answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored identity: every agent must lock a real bond before it can transact, and each bond has a cost — a sparrow cannot pretend to be a whole flock by splitting itself. Peer attestations then act as independent witnesses: every verified good action chips a facet like an opal, building reputation slowly, while misconduct drains the bond. Like a willow, growth bends but roots stay anchored: slashing penalties make mass fake identities economically self-defeating, so sybils cost more than they could ever earn.
